paragraphs.cn: 然而，日本近期的外交言论和行动清楚地暴露出其挑战这一秩序根本底线的危险企图。最近，日本政府悍然要求俄罗斯拆除一座纪念战胜日本军国主义的纪念碑，理由是荒谬的——该纪念碑的设计“伤害了日本人民的感情”。与此同时，日本官员声称《联合国宪章》中的“敌国条款”已经过时，在实践中形同虚设。这些绝非孤立的外交争端，而是日本右翼势力长期以来企图粉饰侵略历史、推翻历史定论的集中表现。作为针对二战战败国的特殊制度安排，“敌国条款”背后的核心法理逻辑是防止法西斯主义和军国主义死灰复燃。它们是国际社会为维护持久和平而设置的政治和法律护栏。

paragraphs.en: The rightward tilt in Japan's political ecology and its drive to become a major military power are inevitably exerting profound impacts on East Asia's security architecture, bringing far-reaching negative consequences to regional peace and stability. At this historical milestone marking the 95th anniversary of the September 18 Incident, the alarm over the possible resurgence of Japanese militarism has rung once again. Japan can never earn the understanding of its Asian neighbors or the respect of the international community through militarism and warmongering.
paragraphs.cn: 日本政治生态的右倾化及其谋求成为军事大国的冲动，不可避免地正在对东亚安全架构产生深远影响，给地区和平与稳定带来深远的负面后果。日本激进的军备扩张，加上指向干预地缘政治争端的政策，已引起亚洲邻国的深切担忧和军事警觉，将地区推入互信受损与军备竞赛的恶性循环。对国际社会而言，听任日本摆脱战后军事约束、制造分裂与对抗，只会破坏亚太地区的繁荣与稳定，进而严重危害全球长期安全。在纪念九一八事变95周年这一历史节点上，日本军国主义可能复活的警钟再次敲响。日本永远无法通过军国主义和好战行径赢得亚洲邻国的理解或国际社会的尊重。

paragraphs.en: To avoid repeating the catastrophic mistakes of history, Japan's only viable path forward is to pull back from the brink, squarely face its past, and engage in profound reflection on its history of aggression. Japan must completely cut ties with lingering militarist ideologies, return to the framework of its Pacifist Constitution, and firmly follow the path of peaceful development. Only by taking concrete actions to honor its commitments to the post-war international order and ceasing to act as a troublemaker in regional affairs can Japan start rebuilding trust with its Asian neighbors and the wider international community.
paragraphs.cn: 为避免重蹈历史的灾难性覆辙，日本唯一可行的前进道路是悬崖勒马，正视过去，深刻反省其侵略历史。日本必须彻底与残存的军国主义意识形态划清界限，回归和平宪法的框架，坚定走和平发展道路。只有以实际行动履行对战后国际秩序的承诺，停止在地区事务中充当麻烦制造者，日本才能开始重建与亚洲邻国及更广泛国际社会的信任。

Editor's note: Xiang Haoyu is a specially appointed research fellow at the Department for Asia-Pacific Studies, China Institute of International Studies. The article reflects the author's opinions and not necessarily the views of CGTN.
September 18 marks the 95th anniversary of the outbreak of the September 18 Incident. The incident not only served as a prelude to Japanese militarism’s brutal invasion of China and other Asian nations, but also destroyed the international system of the time, plunging the entire Asia-Pacific region into the bottomless abyss of war.
At this solemn juncture, a time for deep reflection on wartime tragedies and renewed pledges for peace, a close look at the current situation in East Asia inevitably evokes deep concern.
Recently, a string of unusually dangerous developments have emerged in quick succession within Japan's political and defense circles, such as right-wing conservatives gaining power in local elections, top defense officials openly coveting nuclear armaments and frequent joint regional military drills. and words and deeds that challenge the post-war international order.
All those suggest that Japan's ruling authorities and right-wing factions are accelerating their break from the post-war system and deviating further from the path of peaceful development.
A bell-ringing ceremony is held to mark the 95th anniversary of the September 18 Incident in front of a monument at the September 18 Incident History Museum in Shenyang City, northeast China's Liaoning Province, September 18, 2026. 
Challenging the postwar international order
The post-war international order, with the United Nations at its core, was built precisely upon the defeat of Japanese militarism by the world anti-fascist alliance and hard-won lessons drawn from the war. Nevertheless, Japan's recent diplomatic rhetoric and actions clearly expose a dangerous attempt to challenge the fundamental bottom line of this very order.
Recently, the Japanese government brazenly demanded that Russia dismantle a monument dedicated to the victory over Japanese militarism, citing the absurd justification that the monument's design "hurt the feelings of the Japanese people." Concurrently, Japanese officials have claimed that the "Enemy State Clauses" in the UN Charter are outdated and hollow in practice.
These are by no means isolated diplomatic disputes; rather, they are a concentrated manifestation of the long-standing attempts by Japan's right-wing forces to whitewash its history of aggression and reverse historical verdicts.
As a special institutional arrangement for defeated World War II nations, the core legal logic behind the "Enemy State Clauses" is to prevent the resurgence of fascism and militarism. They constitute political and legal guardrails put in place by the international community to sustain enduring peace.
From the perspective of victimized Asian nations, Japan's demand to remove anti-fascist monuments and its attempt to erase its legal status as a defeated nation amount to an overt provocation against historical justice.
The international community must remain clear-eyed: Japan's regression in historical awareness is not merely a question of passing moral judgment on its past; it is directly tied to the trajectory of its future development. To tolerate historical revisionism from Japan is in essence to shake the foundations of the post-war peace order, which will ultimately harm global peace and stability.
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi gives instructions to senior members of the Japan Self-Defense Forces during an annual meeting at the Defense Ministry in Tokyo, Japan, September 2, 2026. 
The 'broken-window effect' in defense policy
If distortions of history serve as an ideological warning sign, Japan's recent radical leaps in defense policy are manifesting themselves as an increasingly tangible threat.
In the Okinawa gubernatorial election held on September 13, Genta Koja, who received strong backing from the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, won the election. Koja's victory not only signals the forceful push-through of the controversial relocation of the US military base to Henoko; more importantly, it means Tokyo will accelerate the militarization of the Ryukyu Islands, turning them into a bridgehead for intervening in geopolitical conflicts.
An immediate danger posed by this election result is that, in pursuit of military expansion goals, Japan's ruling coalition will press ahead with arming Okinawa, at the risk of dragging the Okinawan people onto the chariot of East-Asian geopolitical conflicts.
Equally alarming is how top defense officials are trampling on peace-oriented bottom lines. Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi recently stated openly that in discussions on revising the three key security documents, no options would be ruled out when considering next-generation submarines, including nuclear-powered ones.
Such remarks represent a blatant betrayal of Japan's long-vaunted Three Non-Nuclear Principles and strip away the government's facade of pursuing an exclusively defense-oriented posture.
Besides, Japan's frequent participation in large-scale joint military exercises in September, such as Freedom Edge 2026 and Orient Shield 2026, shows that the Self-Defense Forces are rapidly transforming from a defensive force into an offensive one equipped with long-range power projection and pre-emptive strike capabilities.
Japan's post-war "exclusively defense-oriented" policy now exists in name only, laying bare a "broken-window effect" that keeps shattering the post-war pacifist system.
Paratroopers with Japan's 1st Airborne Brigade head to the drop zone as US Army air operations managers look on during Operation Orient Shield 2026 Joint Airborne drop at Kita-Dalen Training area in Eniwa, Hokkaido, Japan, September 15, 2026. 
Where is Japan headed?
The rightward tilt in Japan's political ecology and its drive to become a major military power are inevitably exerting profound impacts on East Asia's security architecture, bringing far-reaching negative consequences to regional peace and stability.
Japan's radical arms build-up, paired with policies that point to intervention in geopolitical disputes, has stirred deep concern and military vigilance among its Asian neighbors, pushing the region into a vicious cycle of eroding mutual trust and arms races.
For the international community, allowing Japan to cast off its post-war military constraints to sow division and confrontation will only undermine the prosperity and stability of the Asia-Pacific, which in turn will seriously jeopardize long-term global security.
At this historical milestone marking the 95th anniversary of the September 18 Incident, the alarm over the possible resurgence of Japanese militarism has rung once again. Japan can never earn the understanding of its Asian neighbors or the respect of the international community through militarism and warmongering.
To avoid repeating the catastrophic mistakes of history, Japan's only viable path forward is to pull back from the brink, squarely face its past, and engage in profound reflection on its history of aggression. Japan must completely cut ties with lingering militarist ideologies, return to the framework of its Pacifist Constitution, and firmly follow the path of peaceful development.
Only by taking concrete actions to honor its commitments to the post-war international order and ceasing to act as a troublemaker in regional affairs can Japan start rebuilding trust with its Asian neighbors and the wider international community.

Editor's note: September 18 marks the 95th anniversary of the September 18 Incident, which marked the start of China's war of resistance against Japanese aggression. Xu Weijun is an associate research professor at the Institute of Public Policy, South China University of Technology. His research interests include East Asian international relations and China-US relations. Japan's reckoning with its wartime history has long been a subject of debate, particularly over how the government should confront and acknowledge its past. The article reflects the author's opinions and not necessarily those of CGTN.
In March 2026, an opinion poll conducted by the Japan Broadcasting Corporation revealed a thought-provoking result. When asked whether World War II was "a war of aggression launched by Japan against its Asian neighbors," only 35% of respondents agreed, 16% disagreed, and as many as 48% answered "I don't know." These figures reflect not merely a gap in historical knowledge, but also a deep rupture between war memory and the perception of historical responsibility in contemporary Japanese society.
Contemporary Japanese society does not lack memories of the war. In post-war Japanese public life, there have always been numerous war-related commemorative ceremonies, peace education and narratives of the atomic bombings. At the same time, however, Japanese politicians have repeatedly visited Yasukuni Shrine, which enshrines Class-A war criminals and is widely regarded as a symbol of Japanese militarism and historical revisionism.
This contradictory picture reveals the underlying structure of Japan's war memory: Japanese society remembers the war, and even harbors a genuine fear of it, yet it has not recalled to the same extent how Japan launched the war, how it invaded Asian countries, and how it inflicted enormous suffering on the peoples of those countries. In other words, the current situation in Japanese society is not simply "forgetting the war," but rather "selectively remembering the war."
Many Japanese people can perceive the suffering of war through the atomic bombings, the Battle of Okinawa and the trauma of defeat, yet they may not necessarily understand Japan's responsibility as a perpetrator through the lens of colonial rule, the Nanjing Massacre and the atrocities committed on battlefields in Southeast Asia. For Japanese society, the core issue regarding historical understanding lies not in whether the war is remembered, but in whose suffering is remembered and whose is forgotten.
Candle-lit paper lanterns are floated on the Motoyasu River to commemorate the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Japan, August 6, 2026. 
Structural flaws
This divergence in memory is first related to structural flaws in Japan's history education.
Japanese school education system does not entirely avoid the history of WWII. A 2025 survey of 18-year-olds conducted by the Nippon Foundation found that about 95% of respondents stated they had learned about the "Pacific War," and two-thirds said their memories of the war mainly came from classes in school.
The more critical question, however, is the narrative framework through which this history is presented. The same survey found that among war-themed works that left a deep impression on Japanese youth, Grave of the Fireflies ranked first with 42.2%. This work mainly focuses on the suffering of ordinary Japanese civilians, particularly children, amid air raids and starvation during the final months of WWII.
Such memories of victimhood are not inaccurate; they carry genuine anti-war value. But the problem is that if education about war history mainly revolves around Japanese experiences of victimhood, it can easily lead students to form an intuitive impression that "the war brought suffering to Japan," while making it difficult for them to develop a sense of responsibility that "Japan inflicted profound suffering on Asia."
Japanese youth might be instilled with value judgments such as "war is terrible" and "peace is precious," but they are not sufficiently guided to ask three more fundamental questions: Why did Japan launch the war? How did the peoples of Asian countries bear the consequences of Japanese aggression? Why does post-war Japan need to continue engaging in historical reflection?
'Victim-centered' narrative
Second, public memories of the war in Japanese society have long been characterized by a "victim-centered" narrative. The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the Great Tokyo Air Raid, the Battle of Okinawa, and post-war reconstruction constitute the primary narrative entry points through which the Japanese public perceives the war. The deeper challenge lies beneath these historical memories. When the memory of victimhood is detached from the dimension of perpetrator responsibility, it creates a moral cognitive dislocation: the Japanese public can genuinely perceive the cruelty of war, yet find it difficult to understand why neighboring Asian countries repeatedly demand that Japan reflect on its past. The Japanese society is unwilling to confront Japan's historical identity as an aggressor and perpetrator.
These victim-centered memories have become further entrenched amid generational change. More than 80 years after the war, the number of people with first-hand wartime experience has sharply declined, and direct war memory based on individual experience is gradually fading from Japanese society. Meanwhile, schools, the media, museums, and political discourse have become the primary channels for shaping war memory. Whoever controls these channels is better positioned to determine what Japanese society remembers, what it forgets, and how it understands history.
A Shinto priest leads parliament members to pray for the war dead at Yasukuni war shrine in Tokyo, Japan, April 22, 2026. 
A conservative political landscape
Third, the long-term trend toward political conservatism in Japan has been an important driving force behind the divergence in perceptions of historical responsibility. The political landscape characterized by the Liberal Democratic Party's long-standing dominance has granted right-wing historical perspectives institutional influence far greater than that of left-wing and civic forces engaged in reflection.
Japanese conservative politics does not always directly deny historical facts. Rather, it is more adept at defusing historical responsibility by obscuring narratives and shifting the focus. For example, vague phrasing such as "upholding the positions of previous cabinets" is used to avoid reaffirming an apology, and the argument that "future generations should not be destined to apologize" is employed to cut off the intergenerational continuity of historical responsibility. Through these shifts in discourse, historical responsibility is no longer a moral baseline constraining Japan from repeating past mistakes. Instead, it has been framed as a historical burden hindering Japan's path to becoming a "normal country."
Historical understanding is never merely a debate about the past. It profoundly shapes how a country understands itself, views its neighbors, and chooses its future path. The divergence within Japanese society regarding the nature of the war and historical responsibility appears on the surface as a split in historical narratives. But in essence, it concerns whether post-war Japan can maintain its identity as a peaceful nation through a genuine consciousness of reflection.

这一矛盾图景揭示了日本战争记忆的深层结构：日本社会记得战争，甚至对战争怀有真切的恐惧，但它并未以同等程度回忆日本如何发动战争、如何侵略亚洲国家、如何给这些国家的人民造成巨大苦难。换言之，日本社会的现状并非简单地"遗忘战争"，而是"选择性地记忆战争"。
许多日本人可以通过原子弹爆炸、冲绳战役和战败创伤感知战争的苦难，但他们未必能通过殖民统治、南京大屠杀和东南亚战场暴行的视角理解日本作为加害者的责任。对日本社会而言，历史认知的核心问题不在于是否记得战争，而在于记得谁的苦难、遗忘谁的苦难。2026年8月6日，人们在本安川上放流烛光纸灯笼，纪念美国原子弹轰炸日本广岛81周年。结构性缺陷
这种记忆分歧首先与日本历史教育的结构性缺陷有关。

日本的学校教育体系并非完全回避二战历史。日本财团2025年对18岁年轻人进行的一项调查发现，约95%的受访者表示他们学过"太平洋战争"，三分之二的人表示他们对战争的记忆主要来自学校课堂。然而更关键的问题是呈现这段历史时所采用的叙事框架。同一项调查发现，在对日本年轻人留下深刻印象的战争题材作品中，《萤火虫之墓》以42.2%排名第一。这部作品主要聚焦二战最后几个月空袭和饥饿中普通日本平民尤其是儿童的苦难。

这种受害者记忆并非不准确，它们承载着真实的反战价值。但问题在于，如果战争历史教育主要围绕日本自身的受害经历展开，就容易让学生形成"战争给日本带来了苦难"的直观印象，而难以培养"日本给亚洲造成了深重苦难"的责任意识。
日本年轻人可能被灌输"战争是可怕的""和平是宝贵的"等价值判断，但他们没有被充分引导去追问三个更根本的问题：日本为什么发动战争？亚洲国家的人民如何承受了日本侵略的后果？战后日本为什么需要继续进行历史反思？"以受害者为中心"的叙事
其次，日本社会对战争的公共记忆长期以来具有"以受害者为中心"的叙事特征。

广岛和长崎的原子弹爆炸、东京大空袭、冲绳战役以及战后重建，构成了日本公众感知战争的主要叙事入口。更深层的挑战隐藏在这些历史记忆之下。当受害者记忆与加害者责任维度相脱离时，就会产生一种道德认知错位：日本公众能够真切感知战争的残酷，却难以理解为什么亚洲邻国一再要求日本反思其过去。日本社会不愿正视日本作为侵略者和加害者的历史身份。这些以受害者为中心的记忆在代际更替中进一步固化。

战争结束80多年后，拥有亲历战争经历的人数急剧减少，基于个人经验的直接战争记忆正逐渐从日本社会消退。与此同时，学校、媒体、博物馆和政治话语已成为塑造战争记忆的主要渠道。谁掌控这些渠道，谁就更有能力决定日本社会记住什么、遗忘什么以及如何理解历史。2026年4月22日，在日本东京，一名神道教祭司带领国会议员在靖国神社为战死者祈祷。保守的政治格局
第三，日本政治长期保守化趋势是历史责任认知分歧的重要驱动力。

以自民党长期执政为特征的政治格局，赋予了右翼历史观远大于左翼和公民反思力量的制度性影响力。日本保守政治并不总是直接否认历史事实，而是更擅长通过模糊叙事和转移焦点来消解历史责任。例如，用"坚持历届内阁立场"这类含糊措辞来回避重申道歉，用"后代不应注定道歉"的论调来切断历史责任的代际延续。通过这些话语转换，历史责任不再是约束日本重蹈覆辙的道德底线。

相反，它被塑造成阻碍日本走向"正常国家"的历史包袱。
历史认知从来不只是关于过去的争论。它深刻影响着一个国家如何认识自己、如何看待邻国以及如何选择未来的道路。日本社会在战争性质和历史责任问题上的分歧，表面上表现为历史叙事的分裂，但本质上关乎战后日本能否通过真正的反思意识来维持其和平国家的身份。

articles.title: How telemedicine and smart hospitals are enhancing BRICS healthcare
articles.titleCn: 远程医疗与智慧医院如何提升金砖国家医疗健康水平
articles.summary: Leveraging cutting-edge telemedicine and AI-driven infrastructure, China is advancing high-precision healthcare applications, from 5G-enabled remote ophthalmology to smart public hospitals. These technological breakthroughs are driving deeper multilateral cooperation in BRICS nations, enhancing healthcare accessibility and technical capacity across the Global South.
articles.summaryCn: 中国远程医疗与智慧医院技术日趋成熟，正通过设备输出、基建合作和人才培训等方式加速走向金砖国家等国际医疗合作领域。

Sitting at a surgical console in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, an {{0}} from the Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center tracks a crystal-clear, real-time 5G video feed. A medical team completes the world's first remote robotic subretinal injection between Guangzhou and Xinjiang, marking a landmark progression in remote surgery from centimeter-level precision down to the micron level. /CMG
That robotic arm was deployed in an operating room in Urumqi, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, 4,200 kilometers from the control team in Guangzhou. Lin Haotian, director of the Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center at Sun Yat-sen University, noted that performing such a procedure remotely via robotics marks a clinical {{2}}, as remote robotic interventions of this precision had not previously been documented.
paragraphs.cn: 在广州的手术控制台前，来自中山眼科中心的一位眼科医生注视着清晰实时的5G视频画面。医生操控数千公里外的机械臂，完成精细的视网膜下注射——将靶向药物精准注入患者视网膜下方薄如纸片的组织层中。一支医疗团队在广州与新疆之间完成了全球首例远程机器人视网膜下注射，标志着远程手术从厘米级精度迈向微米级精度的里程碑式进展。/CMG 该机械臂部署在距广州控制团队4200公里的中国西北部新疆维吾尔自治区乌鲁木齐市的一间手术室中。中山大学中山眼科中心主任林浩添指出，通过机器人远程实施此类手术是临床上的一个里程碑，因为此前从未有如此高精度的远程机器人介入手术的记录。

paragraphs.en:
"The retina is only about 100 to 300 micrometers thick, divided into 10 distinct layers. Delivering medication precisely between two of those layers is an exceptionally {{3}} operation," Lin told China Media Group. The adoption of remote medical robotics in China began in 2019 with its first 5G-assisted {{4}} surgery. Over recent years, remote medical procedures have expanded across various {{5}} in Beijing, Shanghai and Zhejiang. From local reach to nationwide networks
These advanced remote procedures reflect a broader expansion of digital health {{6}} across China.
paragraphs.cn: 林浩添在接受中国媒体集团采访时表示：“视网膜厚度仅约100至300微米，分为10个不同的层次。要在其中两层之间精准给药是一项极其精细的操作。”中国远程医疗机器人的应用始于2019年首例5G辅助骨科手术。近年来，远程医疗手术已扩展至北京、上海和浙江的多个专科领域。从本地覆盖到全国网络，这些先进的远程手术反映了中国数字健康基础设施的更广泛扩展。

paragraphs.en:
According to China's National Health Commission, the country's telemedicine network now covers all cities and counties, expanding further into rural communities. Monitoring data shows that 70% of township health centers have established {{7}} telemedicine partnerships with higher-level hospitals. Medical staff review abnormal cells flagged by an AI pathology system at Chongqing University Cancer Hospital in southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, August 26, 2026. /CFP
Alongside the physical infrastructure, AI-driven applications are increasingly {{8}} into daily clinical workflows. At Ruijin Hospital, affiliated with the Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, an AI pathology platform assists doctors by scanning digital slides and highlighting potential {{9}} in seconds – a process that manually takes around 40 minutes per slide.
paragraphs.cn: 据中国国家卫生健康委员会介绍，全国远程医疗网络现已覆盖所有城市和县，并进一步向农村社区延伸。监测数据显示，70%的乡镇卫生院已与上级医院建立了协作性远程医疗合作关系。2026年8月26日，在中国西南部重庆市重庆大学附属肿瘤医院，医务人员正在查看AI病理系统标记的异常细胞。/CFP 除实体基础设施外，人工智能驱动的应用正日益融入日常临床工作流程。在上海交通大学医学院附属瑞金医院，AI病理平台通过扫描数字切片并在数秒内标记潜在病变来辅助医生——而这一过程人工操作每张切片约需40分钟。

paragraphs.en:
Furthermore, a report by KPMG, a global network of professional services firms, indicates that China accounts for over 70% of the world's published medical large language models. As these digital health tools mature domestically, elements of the technology, equipment and operational frameworks are {{10}} being adapted for international healthcare partnerships. Smart infrastructure and clinical applications overseas
As China's telemedicine infrastructure and domestic medical devices continue to mature, these technological solutions are increasingly being incorporated into international healthcare collaborations, particularly across BRICS countries. Construction is underway in São Paulo, Brazil, for the country's first public smart hospital within the University of São Paulo hospital complex. Financed by a $320 million long-term loan from the New Development Bank (NDB) alongside local funding, the 800-bed facility is scheduled to open in 2029.
paragraphs.cn: 此外，全球专业服务公司网络毕马威的一份报告显示，中国占全球已发布医疗大语言模型的70%以上。随着这些数字健康工具在国内日趋成熟，相关技术、设备和运营框架的要素正逐步被调整应用于国际医疗合作。海外智慧基础设施与临床应用 随着中国远程医疗基础设施和国内医疗器械不断成熟，这些技术解决方案正日益被纳入国际医疗合作，尤其是在金砖国家之间。巴西圣保罗正在建设该国首座公立智慧医院，隶属于圣保罗大学医院综合体。该项目由新开发银行提供的3.2亿美元长期贷款及当地资金共同融资，这座拥有800张床位的设施计划于2029年开业。

paragraphs.en:
Developed with technical collaboration from Chinese partners, the project will {{11}} 5G-connected ambulances, AI-assisted {{12}} and automated operational management. NDB President Dilma Rousseff noted that the project serves as a reference model for technology transfer in public health, while Brazilian Minister of Health Alexandre Padilha highlighted the role of international technical collaboration in upgrading public health infrastructure. A clinical team performs a Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation procedure. /CFP
Beyond hospital infrastructure, Chinese medical equipment and diagnostic tools are seeing expanded clinical application overseas. In April 2024, clinical teams from Xiamen Cardiovascular Hospital affiliated to Xiamen University, using Chinese-made medical devices, performed the first local Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) procedures in Brazil and El Salvador.
paragraphs.cn: 该项目在中国合作伙伴的技术协作下开发，将整合5G联网救护车、AI辅助分诊和自动化运营管理。新开发银行行长迪尔玛·罗塞夫指出，该项目是公共卫生领域技术转移的参考模式，而巴西卫生部长亚历山大·帕迪利亚则强调了国际技术协作在升级公共卫生基础设施中的作用。一支临床团队正在实施经导管主动脉瓣植入术。/CFP 除医院基础设施外，中国医疗器械和诊断工具在海外临床应用中也在不断扩大。2024年4月，厦门大学附属厦门心血管医院的临床团队使用国产医疗器械，在巴西和萨尔瓦多完成了当地首例经导管主动脉瓣置换术（TAVR）。

paragraphs.en: By August 2024, teams completed the first TAVR in eastern Indonesia and the country's first Intravascular Lithotripsy (IVL) procedure. In September 2025, the first Chinese-assisted IVL procedure was performed in Vietnam. These {{13}} procedures using innovative equipment reflect an expanding role for domestic medical technologies in international clinical settings. In the commercial biotech sector, a Fujian-based firm established a localized laboratory in São Paulo to provide lower-cost genetic screening for breast cancer – a prevailing health challenge in Brazil. Company records show that partnerships had been established with nearly 20 institutions across BRICS countries by August 2025.
paragraphs.cn: 到2024年8月，团队在印度尼西亚东部完成了首例TAVR以及该国首例血管内碎石术（IVL）。2025年9月，首例中国辅助的IVL手术在越南实施。这些使用创新设备的首次手术反映了国产医疗技术在国际临床环境中日益扩大的作用。在商业生物技术领域，一家福建企业在圣保罗建立了本地化实验室，为巴西普遍存在的健康难题——乳腺癌提供成本更低的基因筛查。公司记录显示，截至2025年8月，已与金砖国家的近20家机构建立了合作关系。

paragraphs.en:
A Chinese surgical team in Shanghai assists in performing Russia's first remote surgery for arrhythmia on a patient at the Meshalkin National Medical Research Center in Novosibirsk using the Stereotaxis robotic magnetic navigation system, March 21, 2025. /CFP
Cultivating talent and strengthening policy dialogues
Beyond medical equipment and infrastructure, human resource development and clinical training remain central to international medical cooperation. The Xiamen Cardiovascular Hospital has established a {{14}} program offering 6-to-12-month clinical training for foreign cardiologists. By October 2025, 28 physicians from 13 countries, including Brazil, Russia, India, Indonesia and Egypt, had been trained. Upon returning to their home institutions, several participants have taken on primary surgical roles, such as performing emergency interventional procedures for acute myocardial infarction.
paragraphs.cn: 2025年3月21日，上海一支中国手术团队使用Stereotaxis机器人磁导航系统，协助在新西伯利亚梅沙尔金国家医学研究中心为一名患者实施俄罗斯首例心律失常远程手术。/CFP 培养人才与加强政策对话 除医疗设备和基础设施外，人力资源开发和临床培训仍是国际医疗合作的核心。厦门心血管医院设立了奖学金项目，为外国心脏病专家提供6至12个月的临床培训。截至2025年10月，已有来自巴西、俄罗斯、印度、印度尼西亚和埃及等13个国家的28名医生接受了培训。返回本国机构后，多名参与者已承担主要手术角色，例如为急性心肌梗死实施急诊介入手术。

paragraphs.en: Official policy frameworks continue to guide these multilateral initiatives. China has participated in the BRICS Health Ministers' Meetings since the inaugural conference in 2011. At the 15th meeting in June 2025, Guo Yanhong, vice minister of China's NHC, noted that China has implemented a health-prioritized development strategy to advance the Healthy China initiative and promote {{15}} governance across medical services, pharmaceuticals and health insurance. China is committed to working alongside BRICS members and partner nations to strengthen policy dialogue, align health actions and deepen exchanges across medical fields, according to Guo.
paragraphs.cn: 官方政策框架继续指导这些多边倡议。中国自2011年首届会议以来一直参加金砖国家卫生部长会议。在2025年6月的第15次会议上，中国国家卫健委副主任郭燕红指出，中国实施了健康优先发展战略，以推进健康中国行动，并促进医疗服务、药品和健康保险的协调治理。据郭燕红介绍，中国致力于与金砖成员国和伙伴国家一道加强政策对话、协调卫生行动并深化医学领域的交流。

On September 16, 2026, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region witnessed something rather special — a milestone event in its modern history: the unveiling of its first five-year plan for economic and social development (2026-2030). Scheduled for fulfillment by the end of the first year of the next decade, this far-sighted programme places especially strong emphasis on the development of the Northern Metropolis — a new cityscape that is anticipated to play a pivotal role in Hong Kong’s spatial and economic landscape in the years to come.
Many viewers may have already encountered the Northern Metropolis from a rather unique vantage point. In 2022, this urban district made a cameo appearance in the CMG documentary Aerial China. For many, that bird’s eye glimpse was sufficient to prompt a question: what exactly was taking shape in northern Hong Kong? Four years on, and the answer is here.
Put simply, the establishment of the Northern Metropolis is intended to address a fundamental issue constraining Hong Kong’s development: limited availability of land. Put another way, growth can only take place if it is possible to accommodate people and industries — in other words, if there is something to grow into.
In this context, the scale of the Northern Metropolis is especially significant. Covering about 30,000 hectares, or roughly one-third of Hong Kong’s total land area, this represents one of the largest ever augmentations to the “inner-space” available for Hong Kong development. For that reason alone, the importance of this new zone is almost impossible to overstate.
But land alone does not create a new economic centre. Infrastructure is what makes development possible. And once again, in this respect, the Northern Metropolis has a distinctive advantage: its location. Situated in Hong Kong’s northern New Territories and directly adjacent to Shenzhen, it sits at the intersection of Hong Kong, and the wider Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The development of the Northern Metropolis therefore goes hand in hand with major investments in transport and cross-boundary connectivity, including the Northern Link and other projects forming part of Hong Kong’s “Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal Corridors” transport network.
But how to make the best of these advantages? The reality is this “winning combination” can only truly be realized with planning and foresight — which is precisely where the newly unveiled five-year plan comes in.
However, the plan does more than simply address issues of infrastructure; it also addresses the task of rebalancing the Hong Kong economy with a view to securing its long-term viability. For the reality is that though Hong Kong’s economy has long been built around several strong pillars, particularly financial services, trade and logistics, and professional services, its industrial structure has relatively limited room for diversification — a point made crystal clear in a speech by Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po at Peking University’s Guanghua School of Management in April.
So, it is in this context that the Northern Metropolis and the new five-year plan are best understood: a comprehensive vision aimed at broadening the economic base of the Hong Kong SAR. Thus, under this five-year plan, it is envisioned not simply as a residential expansion, but as an integrated platform for university education, innovation and technology, industry, and living and working. By bringing universities, research, technology, talent and industries closer together, sectors that have hitherto had less space to develop in Hong Kong will be empowered to flourish.
One thing that should never be underestimated is the scope, scale and ambition of the plan. Over the next five years, the Northern Metropolis is expected to provide not only more than 70,000 housing units but also around one million square meters of commercial floor space — enough to accommodate around 2.5 million people and provide about 650,000 jobs.
As always, the quality of people’s everyday lives lies at the heart of the five-year plan. Creating new industries is a means to an end: the ultimate objective is to create space to live and flourish. By integrating housing, employment, education, transport and community facilities, the Northern Metropolis could help address both the city’s long-standing shortage of space and the need for more diverse employment opportunities.
Seen in this light, the Northern Metropolis is so much more than a development project within Hong Kong’s first five-year plan. In reality, it is nothing less than a physical and spatial platform in which a number of the plan’s ambitions converge: expanding development space, improving connectivity, diversifying the economy, cultivating talent and strengthening links with the Chinese mainland.
And one thing above all is for sure: Hong Kong will continue to draw on its established strengths as an international financial and commercial centre. The essential point is that rather than jettisoning its past strengths, the five-year plan puts Hong Kong in pole position to leverage its unique proximity to Shenzhen and the wider Greater Bay Area to chart a course to future possibilities. In other words, the Northern Metropolis is ideally located in another sense: sitting at the intersection between the successful Hong Kong of the past and the even more successful Hong Kong to come!
With all this in mind, it is perhaps instructive to reflect on that brief clip in Aerial China back in 2022. Back then, little did we know that we were being offered a brief glimpse, a sneak preview, of a much larger story. And now, finally, the curtain is being lifted, and the stage is set for an unfolding drama whose theme will be land, infrastructure, industries, housing, talent and regional connectivity. Who can say precisely what the future holds? To be sure, the five-year plan points the way, but stay tuned to reality to see the Northern Metropolis playing a starring role in the city’s next brilliant chapter.

仅凭这一点，这个新区域的重要性几乎怎么强调都不为过。但仅有土地并不能创造新的经济中心。基础设施才是使发展成为可能的关键。在这方面，北部都会区再次拥有独特优势：其地理位置。它位于香港新界北部，直接毗邻深圳，处于香港与更广阔的粤港澳大湾区的交汇点。

因此，北部都会区的发展与交通和跨境连通性方面的大规模投资齐头并进，包括北环线以及构成香港“八纵八横”交通网络的其他项目。但如何充分利用这些优势？现实是，这种“制胜组合”只有通过规划和远见才能真正实现——而这正是新发布的五年规划的用武之地。然而，该规划不仅仅解决基础设施问题；它还处理重新平衡香港经济以确保其长期可行性的任务。因为现实是，尽管香港经济长期建立在几大支柱之上，尤其是金融服务、贸易物流和专业服务，但其产业结构多元化的空间相对有限——香港财政司司长陈茂波今年4月在北京大学光华管理学院的演讲中明确指出了这一点。

因此，正是在这种背景下，北部都会区和新的五年规划才能得到最好的理解：一个旨在拓宽香港特别行政区经济基础的全面愿景。因此，在这项五年规划下，它不仅仅被设想为住宅扩张，而是一个集大学教育、创新科技、产业以及生活和工作于一体的综合平台。通过将大学、研究、技术、人才和产业更紧密地结合在一起，那些迄今为止在香港发展空间较少的领域将有能力蓬勃发展。有一点绝不应被低估，那就是该规划的范围、规模和雄心。未来五年，北部都会区预计不仅提供超过7万套住房，还将提供约100万平方米的商业楼面面积——足以容纳约250万人并提供约65万个就业岗位。

一如既往，人们的日常生活质量是五年规划的核心。创造新产业是手段而非目的：最终目标是创造生活和繁荣的空间。通过整合住房、就业、教育、交通和社区设施，北部都会区可以帮助解决城市长期存在的空间短缺问题以及对更多样化就业机会的需求。从这个角度看，北部都会区远不止是香港首个五年规划中的一个发展项目。实际上，它不亚于一个实体和空间平台，规划的多项雄心在此汇聚：拓展发展空间、改善连通性、多元化经济、培养人才以及加强与内地的联系。

最重要的是，有一点是肯定的：香港将继续利用其作为国际金融和商业中心的既有优势。关键点在于，五年规划不是抛弃过去的优势，而是让香港处于有利位置，利用其与深圳及更广阔大湾区毗邻的独特优势，开辟通往未来可能性的道路。换句话说，北部都会区在另一种意义上位置理想：它坐落在过去成功的香港与未来更加成功的香港之间的交汇点！考虑到这一切，回顾2022年《航拍中国》中的那段简短片段或许是有启发性的。那时，我们几乎不知道，我们看到的只是一个更大故事的短暂一瞥、一个先睹为快。

而现在，帷幕终于拉开，舞台已经搭好，一场以土地、基础设施、产业、住房、人才和区域连通性为主题的戏剧即将展开。谁能准确说出未来会怎样？可以肯定的是，五年规划指明了方向，但请继续关注现实，看北部都会区在这座城市下一个辉煌篇章中扮演主角。

articles.fullText:
A surgical robot developed by Surgerii Robotics is exhibited at the 93rd China International Medical Equipment Fair (CMEF) in Shanghai, China, April 9, 2026. 
In a Barcelona operating room this summer, a 12-year-old boy with multiple kidney stones and organ damage became part of an unlikely trade story. Surgeons at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, one of Spain's top public hospitals, removed the damaged tissue through a single incision barely 2.5 centimeters wide, guided from a console by a surgical robot designed and built in Beijing.
Three snake-shaped instruments and a 3D camera, mounted on nickel-titanium arms, reached the surgical site through that single opening. The boy went home within 48 hours. According to the hospital, it was the first pediatric surgery in Europe performed with a single-incision robot.
The machine was a single-port surgical robot from Beijing-based Surgerii Robotics, delivered under a 2.42-million-euro contract – the highest price yet recorded for a Chinese-built surgical robot sold abroad – and above the European price of the US market leader's mainstream system. Bidding against the US giant's own single-port system, the Chinese robot met the hospital's tender terms within 30 days: installation and revalidation, training for 10 lead surgeons in five departments, and 11 operations.
The Barcelona deal is one data point in a broader shift: in the first half of 2026, China exported 480 million yuan ($71 million) of surgical robots, 3.3 times a year earlier, with export markets growing from 23 countries and regions to 49, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC).
From boxes to blueprints
China's export mix is shifting as fast as its trade in volumes. Surgerii's robot relies on a self-developed "snake arm" that bends at multiple angles and filters out a surgeon's natural hand tremor; over 95% of its components are made in China, cutting costs to roughly half to one-third of foreign rivals.
A parallel story is unfolding on factory floors. In Shenzhen, Bambu Lab's desktop 3D printers have become fixtures in workshops from Mexico to Brazil, where small manufacturers build flexible, small-batch production lines without heavy upfront investment. China exported 3.62 million 3D printers in the first half, up 90.2%, with export value surging 109.3% to 9.61 billion yuan, customs data show.
Students operate teaching equipment for the artificial intelligence program at the Luban Workshop at L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University in Astana, Kazakhstan, May 22, 2026. /Xinhua
Filling gaps, not crowding markets
Much of the new demand comes from places where established Western vendors have long had little presence.
In Astana, Kazakhstan, 20-year-old student Zhansaya Abdurakhman is learning computer vision and robotic-arm operation inside the Luban Workshop, a Chinese-backed vocational training program where China's Tianjin Vocational Institute has set up an AI training center with L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University. "These skills are in great demand," she told Xinhua. The workshop has already trained nearly 100 teachers and over 30 students. In May, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree bringing AI into secondary schools nationwide, including a pilot to narrow the urban-rural education gap.
China's intelligent water management tools are also reaching climate-stressed countries. At the 2025 Great Rivers Forum in Wuhan, an AI flood early-warning platform drew interest from UNESCO's Humid Tropics Centre in Kuala Lumpur, which is studying China's "sponge city" approach, a way of designing cities to absorb and reuse rainwater, for Malaysia's intensifying rainfall. Chinese-built water projects in Pakistan, Guinea and Sudan have improved water and electricity access for millions.
The trade flows are substantial. China's trade with Belt and Road partners rose 14.8% in the first half to 12.97 trillion yuan – just over half its total – while trade with Africa grew 19.6% and with Latin America 16.2%; high-tech exports climbed 39%.
Staff members track operations through a digital twin system in the control room of the COSCO Shipping Ports Abu Dhabi Terminal. /People's Daily
Built with the world
At Khalifa Port in Abu Dhabi, a container terminal jointly built and operated by COSCO Shipping Ports and Abu Dhabi Ports has grown into one of the Gulf's busiest hubs since its December 2018 opening. In 2024 it handled 1.845 million TEUs, or twenty-foot equivalent units, up 36%, with more than 1,000 vessel calls. Its general manager says continuous intelligent upgrading has made it "the smartest terminal in the Middle East."
The project reads like a global supply chain in miniature: quay cranes from Shanghai crane maker ZPMC, electrical automation from Germany's Siemens, and systems integration from China.
In Malaysia, a joint venture between Chinese industrial-internet firm GYMD and local partner Altel Group – witnessed by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim – has become the country's first end-to-end digital service provider for the automotive value chain. At national carmaker Proton's plant, its Geega platform – industrial software that digitally manages entire factory floors – links manufacturing and procurement; a BRICS smart-manufacturing solutions catalogue released this year credits it with cutting equipment downtime by 10-20%.
The macro numbers point the same way. China's imports grew 22.1% in the first half of 2026 – 8.7 percentage points faster than its exports – and contributed more to trade growth than exports did, the GAC said.
Back in Barcelona, the boy's two-day recovery was a human thread in a much larger story. As GAC Deputy Administrator Wang Jun put it, China's stable supply chains are becoming "a key hub connecting all parties in win-win cooperation."

一台由术锐机器人公司研发的手术机器人在2026年4月9日于中国上海举办的第93届中国国际医疗器械博览会上展出。今年夏天，在巴塞罗那的一间手术室里，一名患有多种肾结石和器官损伤的12岁男孩成为了一则看似不可能的贸易故事的一部分。西班牙顶级公立医院之一——瓦尔·德希伯伦大学医院的外科医生通过一个仅2.5厘米宽的单一切口切除了受损组织，整个过程由一台在北京设计和制造的手术机器人从控制台进行引导。三个蛇形器械和一台3D摄像头安装在镍钛合金臂上，通过那个单一开口到达手术部位。男孩在48小时内就回了家。

据该医院称，这是欧洲首例使用单孔机器人进行的儿科手术。这台机器是总部位于北京的术锐机器人公司生产的单孔手术机器人，以242万欧元的合同交付——这是中国制造的手术机器人在海外销售中记录到的最高价格——且高于美国市场领导品牌主流系统在欧洲的售价。在与美国巨头自家单孔系统的竞标中，这台中国机器人在30天内满足了医院的招标条件：安装和重新验证、为五个科室的10名主刀外科医生提供培训，以及11台手术。巴塞罗那的这笔交易只是更大转变中的一个数据点：据海关总署数据，2026年上半年，中国出口了4.8亿元人民币（7100万美元）的手术机器人，是去年同期的3.3倍，出口市场从23个国家和地区增长到49个。从箱子到蓝图，中国的出口结构正与其贸易量的变化一样迅速地转变。

术锐的机器人依靠自主研发的“蛇形臂”，它可以在多个角度弯曲，并过滤掉外科医生自然的手部颤抖；其超过95%的零部件在中国制造，将成本降至外国竞争对手的大约二分之一到三分之一。类似的故事正在工厂车间上演。在深圳，拓竹科技的桌面3D打印机已成为从墨西哥到巴西各地工作坊的常见设备，那里的小型制造商无需大量前期投资就能建立灵活的小批量生产线。海关数据显示，中国上半年出口了362万台3D打印机，增长90.2%，出口额激增109.3%至96.1亿元。学生们在鲁班工坊操作人工智能课程的教学设备。

2026年5月22日，哈萨克斯坦阿斯塔纳，古米廖夫欧亚国立大学。/新华社 填补空白，而非挤占市场。许多新需求来自西方老牌供应商长期以来鲜有涉足的地方。在哈萨克斯坦阿斯塔纳，20岁的学生詹萨娅·阿卜杜拉赫曼正在鲁班工坊内学习计算机视觉和机械臂操作。鲁班工坊是一个中国支持的职业培训项目，中国的天津职业院校与古米廖夫欧亚国立大学合作在那里设立了一个人工智能培训中心。“这些技能需求很大，”她告诉新华社。

该工坊已经培训了近100名教师和30多名学生。5月，总统卡西姆若马尔特·托卡耶夫签署法令，将人工智能引入全国中学，包括一项旨在缩小城乡教育差距的试点。中国的智能水资源管理工具也在进入受气候压力影响的国家。在2025年于武汉举办的大河论坛上，一个人工智能洪水预警平台引起了吉隆坡联合国教科文组织湿润热带中心的兴趣，该中心正在研究中国的“海绵城市”方法——一种通过设计城市来吸收和再利用雨水的方式——以应对马来西亚日益加剧的降雨。中国在巴基斯坦、几内亚和苏丹建设的水利项目已改善了数百万人的供水和供电条件。

贸易流量十分可观。中国与共建“一带一路”伙伴的贸易上半年增长14.8%，达到12.97万亿元——略超过其总额的一半——而与非洲的贸易增长19.6%，与拉丁美洲的贸易增长16.2%；高科技出口攀升39%。工作人员在阿布扎比中远海运港口码头的控制室里通过数字孪生系统跟踪运营情况。/人民日报 与世界共建。在阿布扎比的哈利法港，由中远海运港口和阿布扎比港务局共同建设和运营的集装箱码头自2018年12月开业以来，已发展成为海湾地区最繁忙的枢纽之一。2024年，它处理了184.5万标准箱（即二十英尺标准箱），增长36%，停靠船舶超过1000艘次。

其总经理表示，持续的智能化升级使其成为“中东最智能的码头”。该项目读起来就像全球供应链的缩影：来自上海起重机制造商振华重工的岸桥、来自德国西门子的电气自动化，以及来自中国的系统集成。在马来西亚，中国工业互联网公司GYMD与当地合作伙伴Altel集团的合资企业——在总理安瓦尔·易卜拉欣的见证下——已成为该国首个面向汽车价值链的端到端数字服务提供商。在国产汽车制造商宝腾的工厂，其Geega平台——一种对整个工厂车间进行数字化管理的工业软件——连接了制造和采购；今年发布的一份金砖国家智能制造解决方案目录称赞其将设备停机时间减少了10%至20%。宏观数据也指向同一方向。海关总署表示，2026年上半年中国进口增长22.1%——比出口快8.7个百分点——对贸易增长的贡献超过出口。

回到巴塞罗那，男孩两天的康复是一个更大故事中的人性线索。正如海关总署副署长王军所说，中国稳定的供应链正在成为“连接各方合作共赢的关键枢纽”。
